Name: Balthasar Hubmaier
Summary: German theologian (1480-1528) and former Catholic priest who became the most learned early defender of believer's baptism.
Contribution: He wrote extensively for believer's baptism, religious freedom, and a free church, and led Anabaptist congregations in Waldshut and Moravia. His writings gave the early Anabaptist movement theological weight beyond its Swiss origins.
KeyWorks: On the Christian Baptism of Believers
Testimony: He was burned at the stake in Vienna, and his wife was drowned in the Danube days later.
